label: prop:confined-knot-binding
title: Confined knot binding mechanism: character ratio decomposition per jet level
html:
Let \beta \in H_3(R, q) be a confined nuclear braid built from crossing operators at generators \sigma_{i_k}. The Wedderburn-Artin decomposition separates each crossing's contribution into three channels:

  \hat{V}(c, d)
  = W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{sym}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{std}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{alt}}(c, d).

The extremal contributions exactly cancel for symmetric crossings encoding the proton-neutron force. The binding volume transfers entirely to the standard representation:

  \hat{V}_{\mathrm{pn}}
  = W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \Bigl(z - \frac{h_{\mathrm{A}}}{2}\Bigr).

The 2-dimensional standard representation creates non-commuting cross-channel interactions between adjacent generators. This generates the Markov-weighted pair interaction term \delta_{\times}.

For an A-nucleon system constructed sequentially through quark, nucleon, and nuclear jet levels, the character ratio measures the volume departure from the free constituents. The total knot factor multiplies these strict, empirically-independent character ratios across all levels.

The three levels are not in one convention

The product "across all levels" needs the three character ratios to be ratios of the same functional. They are not. The quark and nucleon levels are Markov traces — weights y_\lambda, convention D (Wenzl r = 2), which admits only \le 2-row shapes. The nuclear-jet level is specified by \tilde w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[n]_q!, over all partitions, and those are distinct families on every stratum. On H_3:

\lambda y_\lambda (D) \tilde w_\lambda
(3) 0.505404226503931 0.163383228056257
(2,1) 0.247297886748035 0.660673773661173
(1,1,1) 0 0.163383228056257

\sum_\lambda \dim(\lambda)\,y_\lambda = 1 exactly, as a normalised trace must; \sum_\lambda \tilde w_\lambda = 0.98744 at q_0. The (1,1,1) row is structural — convention D is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 point of the Ocneanu family, so y_\lambda = 0 once \lambda has more than two rows, while \tilde w is a ratio of positive quantum integers. The jet measure charges a block the Markov trace annihilates.

The two disagree about the pn bond in particular, and not by a rescale: the single interface letter traces to z + d_{pn} = 0.508229789376739 under y, and to 0.000071511999729 under \tilde w — a factor of 7107, because \tilde w weights the two blocks equally and d_{pn} is their midpoint up to \delta, making pn its near-null vector.

Together with the A \ge 3 ill-posedness of the jet word (measured), the three-level product is not evaluable as written. Either obstruction alone suffices. the_nuclear_jet_level_is_the_retired_all_pairs_object_probe.py.
